newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark builds base before test to upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark builds base before test to upside.

text.p: The dollar dug a secure foothold at 1.7080/90 marks after Tuesday's impressive 200 point rise, readying for an attempt to best last week's three-year peak at 1.7375 marks, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
"(Dlr/mark) moves higher pretty soon, otherwise it sinks under its own weight," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.
However, before revisiting its recent top, the greenback must topple resistance at 1.7180 and 1.7210 marks, above which numerous stop-loss buy orders are located, chartists said.
Dealers said from this point forward, the dollar must close above the the 1.7080/90 prop to keep Tuesday's momentum intact.
The 1.7080/90 zone was the start of the dollar/mark breakdown four days ago which took the U.S. unit to a two-week low of 1.6950 marks on Monday, which now provides downside support.

Against the yen, the dollar was consolidative around 126 with overnight gains capped by 126.40/50 resistance and losses supported by a floor at 125.80 that should prevent a retest of the 125.10 yen low seen on Monday.
"A move past 126.45 yen would lead to a retest of the April 10 high at 127.16," said a analyst at a U.S. bank.
Sterling fell sharply on Wednesday, crashing through support at $1.6310 and testing sub-$1.62 waters before settling above the figure.
"Any time a market has a good opportunity to move higher and doesn't take advantage of it, it's going to come off and that's exactly what happened," Tirone said.
